attempts.diagnosis: The gcd function only requires m > 0, so n can be 0. If n == 0 and m > 0, the recursive call gcd(m - n, n) is gcd(m, 0) again, which does not decrease any termination measure, so Dafny cannot prove termination. Adding n > 0 to the function precondition ensures both arguments stay positive and the subtraction branches strictly decrease.
